items.title: 73243_Joe Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Nathan B. Young was the president then at that time. And, I got the real treatment.

ctx.x: Well, you didn't want to play the bass anyway.

I didn't want to march. I didn't want to play the trumpet really. I had enough of that marching business so I didn't show. So then I was called into the president's office and Nathan B. Young was the president then at that time. And, I got the real treatment. So I told him, "Well, Mr. President, this is my instrument. The trumpet is my instrument

and I don't care for the ROTC in the first place. And I don't care to march and I know nothing at all about the bass." He said, "Mr. Thomas, you'll have to cooperate." I said, "I am the best of cooperating, Mr. President, to/my knowledge." He said, "What did you do?" I said, "I stayed at home. Stayed in my dormitory." He said, "That won't do at all."
